basic_information.short_title: Datu Alawaddin T. Bandon, Sr. Memorial Hospital Upgrade
basic_information.official_title: AN ACT UPGRADING THE DATU ALAWADDIN T. BANDON, SR. MEMORIAL HOSPITAL IN THE MUNICIPALITY OF SIBUTU, PROVINCE OF TAWI-TAWI, FROM A TEN-BED CAPACITY INFIRMARY TO A TWENTY-FIVE-BED CAPACITY LEVEL I GENERAL HOSPITAL, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
signed_by: Prof. Raby B. Angkal, Secretary General
basic_information.effectivity: 15 days after publication in the Official Gazette or a newspaper of regional circulation

citizen_summary.what_is_this_about: Upgrades a 10-bed island infirmary in Sibutu, Tawi-Tawi into a 25-bed Level I general hospital — and requires its annual report on operations, spending and outcomes to be made publicly accessible.
citizen_summary.why_was_it_proposed: The hospital was created by a 1990 national law as a 10-bed municipal facility. The act raises it to Level I standards, modernises its record systems, and corrects a location problem created when its host municipality was split.
citizen_summary.what_will_change: Capacity rises to 25 beds at Level I. Facilities and professional manpower are upgraded, the patient information system is modernised for data sharing between departments, and the hospital administrator must publish an annual report.
who_will_be_affected: Patients whose records move between departments and doctors
Hospital staff, through new plantilla positions
Local government units, which receive a copy of the annual report
citizen_summary.when_will_it_take_effect: In force since 2025 — 15 days after publication.

what_this_means_for_you.in_short: NOW LAW. A 10-bed infirmary becomes a 25-bed Level I hospital, with a modernised patient record system and an annual report that must be made public.
in_practice: 10-bed municipal hospital becomes a Level I general hospital with 25 beds, to Ministry of Health standards
Existing facilities and professional manpower upgraded and expanded to Level I standards
The patient information system is streamlined for comprehensive records in a simplified format, with data sharing across departments
MOH with the finance ministry determines and approves the organisational structure and plantilla positions
MOH, the Ministry of Interior and Local Government and the concerned LGUs must cooperate to enhance local health services
The hospital administrator submits an annual report on operations, performance, financial expenditures and service delivery outcomes — copied to LGUs and made publicly accessible

for_specific_groups.Patients: 25 beds instead of 10, and a record system built so your information moves between the doctors treating you.
for_specific_groups.Anyone tracking the hospital: Section 8 is unusually strong — the annual report covers operations, performance, financial expenditures and service delivery outcomes, and must be publicly accessible.
for_specific_groups.Local government: You receive a copy of the annual report, and the health and interior ministries must coordinate with you on local health services.
for_specific_groups.Anyone confused about the address: The hospital was created by law in Sitangkai; after Sibutu was carved out of Sitangkai, it now sits in Sibutu. Section 2 records this.

what_this_means_for_you.when_you_will_feel_it: In force since 2025; delivery depends on the appropriation being released.
what_you_can_do: Ask for the hospital's annual report — Section 8 requires it to be publicly accessible
Ask your LGU, which also receives a copy
watch_out_for: No completion deadline for the upgrade.
Future expansion depends on an MOH recommendation and the availability of funds.

key_terms_explained.Infirmary: A small facility below hospital classification — here 10 beds.
key_terms_explained.Level I general hospital: A basic hospital with emergency care, general medicine and a ward.
key_terms_explained.Plantilla positions: Permanent, funded posts in the government staffing structure.
key_terms_explained.RA 6853: The 1990 national law creating the hospital.
key_terms_explained.MMA Act No. 197: The ARMM-era law that created the Municipality of Sibutu out of Sitangkai.

what_this_means_for_you.status_note: Passed Dhu Al-Hijjah 20, 1446 / 16 June 2025, approved by Chief Minister Abdulraof A. Macacua on 9 July 2025.

benefits.headline: A 25-bed Level I hospital for an island municipality, with a public annual report.

direct_benefits.benefit: 25 beds at Level I instead of a 10-bed infirmary
A publicly accessible annual report on operations, spending and outcomes
direct_benefits.how_to_access: Section 8 — submitted to MOH, copied to LGUs, made publicly accessible

for_citizens: None. The act imposes no duty on the public.

what_is_prohibited: The act defines no prohibited acts and creates no offences.

penalties.for_citizens: None. The act creates no offence, fine or imprisonment.

where_to_complain.oversight: Ministry of Health – BARMM, which supervises and monitors administration and management; the concerned LGUs receive the annual report
where_to_complain.note: The act creates no complaints procedure, but the annual report is public by law.

everyday_scenarios: A patient in Sibutu previously had a 10-bed infirmary; the upgrade authorises a 25-bed Level I hospital.
A resident wants to know how the hospital spent its money. Section 8 requires an annual report covering financial expenditures and service delivery outcomes, made publicly accessible.
Someone searching for the hospital's legal address finds it created in Sitangkai — Section 2 explains that Sibutu was later created out of Sitangkai, so the hospital now sits in Sibutu.

key_provisions: Section 1 — Records that the hospital was established by Republic Act No. 6853 as a 10-bed municipal hospital in Sitangkai, Tawi-Tawi, on 24 February 1990.
Section 2 — Notes that with the enactment of Muslim Mindanao Autonomy Act No. 197, which created the Municipality of Sibutu from Sitangkai, the hospital is now located in Sibutu.

Section 3 — Upgrades the hospital from a 10-bed municipal hospital to a Level I general hospital with 25-bed capacity, in accordance with Ministry of Health standards, integrating the relevant provisions of Republic Act 11223, the Universal Health Care Act.

Section 4 — Existing health service facilities and professional manpower are upgraded and expanded to comply with Level I standards and to align operating systems with current advancements in science and technology. The hospital's information system shall be streamlined to maintain comprehensive patient records in a simplified and easily comprehensible format, enabling seamless data sharing and synchronisation among doctors and authorised personnel across departments and offices.

Section 5 — The MOH, coordinating with the Ministry of Finance, and Budget and Management, determines and approves the organisational structure and plantilla positions, and supervises and monitors the hospital's administration and management.

Section 6 — The MOH, the Ministry of Interior and Local Government and the concerned local government units shall cooperate and coordinate to further enhance the delivery of health services in their locality.

Section 7 — The MOH may recommend to the Chief Minister and the Bangsamoro Parliament further expansion of the hospital's facilities, services or bed capacity based on evolving healthcare needs, subject to the availability of funds.

Section 8 — The hospital administrator shall submit an annual report to the MOH detailing operations, performance, financial expenditures and service delivery outcomes. A copy shall also be submitted to the concerned LGUs. All such reports shall be made publicly accessible.
Section 9 — An initial ₱50,000,000 is charged against the 2025 General Appropriations Act of the Bangsamoro, with operations thereafter in the annual appropriations.
Section 12 — Takes effect 15 days after publication in the Official Gazette or a newspaper of regional circulation.

who_benefits: Patients and clinicians using the hospital's records
impact.figures_note: Quoted from Sections 3 and 9: 10 beds to 25, ₱50,000,000 initial.

citizen_questions.q: How much bigger is the hospital?
citizen_questions.a: From a 10-bed municipal facility to a Level I general hospital with 25 beds.

citizen_questions.q: Can I see how it performs?
citizen_questions.a: Yes. Section 8 requires an annual report on operations, performance, financial expenditures and service delivery outcomes, copied to local government units and made publicly accessible.

citizen_questions.q: Why does the founding law say Sitangkai?
citizen_questions.a: The hospital was created there by Republic Act 6853 in 1990. Muslim Mindanao Autonomy Act No. 197 later created the Municipality of Sibutu out of Sitangkai, so the hospital now sits in Sibutu. Section 2 records this.
Section 4 requires the information system to be streamlined for comprehensive patient records in a simplified format, with data shared across departments and among the doctors treating you.
